metadata.note: Toledo and Ohio Central Railway (1885-1921), its predecessor the Ohio Central Railroad (1880-1884 drawable), and the New York Central's operation of the T&OC as the 'Ohio Central Lines' from 1 Jan 1922: Toledo - Findlay - Kenton - Columbus, Columbus - Corning (meeting the Kanawha and Michigan layer), the Eastern Division Toledo - Fostoria - Bucyrus - Granville - Thurston, and the St. Marys branch. Drawn spans follow the report's drawable: fields exactly. Research report: research report research/branches/toledo_and_ohio_central_railway.txt.
metadata.operator_split: Rule 4 splits: 1885 Ohio Central -> T&OC (foreclosure reorganisation; 1885 itself undrawn); 1 Jan 1922 T&OC -> New York Central (lease). Ohio Central and T&OC features carry new colours used by no other company; NYC-era features carry the existing New York Central colour pulled programmatically from data/. Not splits: Hocking Valley / Morgan-combination stock control, the 1910 Lake Shore stock judgment, USRA 1918-20, the 1938 and 1952 mergers.

segments.note: T&OC era. Starts 1893: the T&OC bought the Toledo, Columbus & Cincinnati in 1892 (american-rails.com), but the first T&OC-era passenger-guide evidence is Fowler's z (1893G) letters at Yondota Street, Hobart, Mungen, Trombley, North Findlay, Eagle Creek and others; 1892 is plausible but not confirmed. Fowler a (1905G) at virtually every station; Perrysburg Journal 5 Oct 1906 advertises Ohio Central Lines parlor/cafe through trains to Columbus, Athens, Middleport, Gallipolis and Charleston. Ends 31 Dec 1921 as an operator era only: the T&OC was leased to the New York Central on 1 Jan 1922 (PRR chronology; Wikipedia and american-rails give 1928 - conflict recorded in metadata); service continues as nyc-toc-toledo-columbus. Earlier operators of Toledo - Findlay - Kenton (Toledo & Indianapolis / TC&S / TC&C, 1884-1891 evidence) are not drawn because the operator for each year is not established. Headway is an estimate, not sourced. About three trains each way a day assumed.

Fowler z (1893G) and a (1905G) along the line; 1906 through trains Toledo - Columbus - Athens - Middleport - Gallipolis - Charleston (Perrysburg Journal). Ends 31 Dec 1921 as an operator era only (NYC lease 1 Jan 1922 - see metadata); continues as nyc-toc-columbus-corning. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

Service was discontinued 25 Jan 1950, restored by Ohio PUC order 25 Mar 1950, and the last run of Nos. 5-6 - using trackage rights on the PRR Zanesville Branch between New Lexington and Bremen - was 17 Jun 1950, ending T&OC passenger service between Columbus and Charleston (PRR chronology 1950). The Feb 1952 Guide index still lists Rendville, Rushville and Thurston under NYC Table 33 - stale, not evidence of service. Freight continued. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

segments.note: Ohio Central Railroad era (receivership from 1883 is the same railroad, not a split). Starts 1880: Fowler former names Bush's (Thurston), Schneider's (Harley), Rends (Rendville) and Tunnel Siding, all 1880G; earlier 1879G names near Clay Bank may be the Columbus & Sunday Creek Valley's own operation, so 1879 is not drawn. Ends 1884: q (1884G) at Burt's (Truro), Brice's, Pickering (Pickerington) and Ferrara confirm 1884; the 1885 reorganisation as the T&OC is of unknown month, so 1885 is left undrawn on both sides. The C&SCV completed the A&LE's Moxahala tunnel and built north to Columbus (american-rails.com). Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

No Toledo - Granville figure is documented; the checks are Toledo - Bucyrus traced 69.6 mi against 69.5 mi (Fowler route 19), and Bucyrus - Granville 60.3 mi, which with Granville - Thurston gives Bucyrus - Thurston 79.9 mi against 78.4 documented. Draws the original T&OC line through Mount Gilead, correct for this era (the 1924 move into the Big Four station is after it). LATER ALIGNMENT not checked beyond that.

segments.note: T&OC era on the original Ohio Central main line, Toledo - Fostoria - Bucyrus - Mount Gilead - Centerburg - Johnstown - Granville. Starts 1888: first T&OC-era guide evidence Smith's Siding and Broken Sword, 7/1888G (Fowler). Fowler z (1893G) at Lakeside; Fowler gives this route no 1905G letters (a Fowler gap, not absence). Perrysburg Journal 3 Aug 1906: 'Ohio Central Home-Coming Excursion ... $1.00 to Bucyrus, $1.25 to Mt. Gilead and Centerburg, $1.00 to Granville ... Train from Toledo (O. C. depot)' - a passenger train over the whole stretch in 1906. Passenger service confirmed to 1906 [OPEN]. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when T&OC service on this stretch actually stopped (continuity 1907-1921 is inferred only from NYC-era evidence south of Bucyrus). Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

EARLIER ALIGNMENT AT MOUNT GILEAD: from 1924 NYC trains were rerouted into the Big Four (CCC&StL) station at Mount Gilead (Fowler); this feature draws the original T&OC line through the town for 1922-1935, so 1924-1935 is drawn ~1 km off the station actually used.

segments.note: New York Central (Ohio Central Lines) era on the Eastern Division south of Bucyrus, from the 1 Jan 1922 lease (conflict with 1928 recorded in metadata). From 1924 trains were rerouted into the Big Four station at Mount Gilead (Fowler: 'Mount Gilead (TOC) (until 1924)', 'Mount Gilead (CCCStL) (from 1924, reverse)') - positive evidence of passenger trains Bucyrus - Centerburg after 1924. Ends 1935: 'April 27, 1935 was the day that the last passenger service traveled through the Johnstown Depot' (Johnstown Historical Society). Whether the rest of the line lost its trains the same day is not established; by 1951 all of Toledo - Thurston was 'Freight Service only' (Feb 1952 Guide Table 138). Freight continued (south of Bucyrus to 1965, Johnstown abandoned 1976) - none of that is a passenger year. Toledo - Bucyrus is NOT drawn for the NYC era: no passenger evidence after 1906. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

segments.note: Ohio Central Railroad era on its original main line Toledo - Fostoria - Bucyrus - Granville - Thurston. The first train passed Johnstown on 4 Jul 1880 (Johnstown Historical Society), but a first train is not necessarily a passenger train, so 1880 is not drawn. Starts 1881: Fowler former names Freeport (Wayne), Petersburg (Deunquat), Locust (Martel), Levering (Edison), Lincoln Centre (Fulton), Fowlerton (Peerless) and P. H. Crossing (Heath), all 1881G, spanning the whole line. Ends 1884: q (1884G) at Kremlin (Wayne), Hartford (Croton), McCutchinsville; the 1885 reorganisation as the T&OC (month unknown) leaves 1885 undrawn. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

segments.note: Peoria - East Liberty - Bellefontaine - Russells Point - Wapakoneta - St. Marys. [ANCHOR] single proven year: in 1904 the Bellefontaine Republican (7 Jun, 8 Jul) ran 'Ohio Central Excursions' ads for its Bellefontaine agent (tickets to Lima, Athens, Toledo, Wapakoneta, Detroit; 'train leaving Bellefontaine at 8:15 a.m.'), and the New Bremen Stern des Westlichen Ohio (7 Jul 1904) advertised Sunday excursions to Columbus 'über die Ohio Central Linien'. Excursions count as passenger service. Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed - opening year, regular-service years and end are all unknown (freight only by 1951, Feb 1952 Guide Table 133). Do not widen this anchor without evidence. Headway is a placeholder, not sourced (excursion trains).
